    def build_attestation_params(challenge:)
      credential_id = SecureRandom.random_bytes(32)
      auth_data = build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id: credential_id)

      {
        passkey: {
          client_data_json: webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.create"),
          attestation_object: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX + auth_data, padding: false),
          transports: [ "internal" ]
        }
      }
    end

    def build_assertion_params(challenge:, credential:, sign_count: 1)
      client_data_json = webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.get")
      authenticator_data = build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count: sign_count)
      signature = webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)

      {
        passkey: {
          id: credential.credential_id,
          client_data_json: client_data_json,
          authenticator_data: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(authenticator_data, padding: false),
          signature: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(signature, padding: false)
        }
      }
    end

    def webauthn_client_data_json(challenge:, type:)
      { challenge: challenge, origin: "http://www.example.com", type: type }.to_json
    end

    # Attestation auth data includes the attested credential (public key + credential ID).
    def build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),   # rp_id_hash
        [ 0x45 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV + AT
        [ 0 ].pack("N"),                            # sign_count
        "\x00" * 16,                                # aaguid
        [ credential_id.bytesize ].pack("n"),       # credential_id_length
        credential_id,
        COSE_PUBLIC_KEY
      ].join.b
    end

    # Assertion auth data is simpler — no attested credential.
    def build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),
        [ 0x05 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV
        [ sign_count ].pack("N")
      ].join.b
    end

    def webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)
      signed_data = authenticator_data + Digest::SHA256.digest(client_data_json)
      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY.sign("SHA256", signed_data)
    end

require "test_helper"

class I18nCompletenessTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "available locales and default locale configuration" do
    assert_equal :en, I18n.default_locale
    assert_equal %i[ en ja ], I18n.available_locales
  end

  test "en.yml and ja.yml have matching keys and matching interpolations" do
    en = flatten_translations(YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/en.yml")).fetch("en"))
    ja = flatten_translations(YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/ja.yml")).fetch("ja"))

    missing_in_ja = en.keys - ja.keys
    assert_empty missing_in_ja, "Keys present in en.yml but missing in ja.yml: #{missing_in_ja.inspect}"

    en.each do |key, en_val|
      ja_val = ja[key]
      next unless en_val.is_a?(String) && ja_val.is_a?(String)
      next if key == "signups.account_name.nth"

      en_vars = en_val.scan(/%\{(\w+)\}/).flatten.uniq.sort
      ja_vars = ja_val.scan(/%\{(\w+)\}/).flatten.uniq.sort
      assert_equal en_vars, ja_vars, "Interpolation mismatch for #{key}"
    end
  end

  test "static error pages render in both English and Japanese" do
    %w[
      400.html
      404.html
      406-unsupported-browser.html
      422.html
      500.html
    ].each do |filename|
      html = File.read(Rails.root.join("public", filename))
      assert_includes html, "Back home", "Expected English back link in #{filename}"
      assert_includes html, "ホームに戻る", "Expected Japanese back link in #{filename}"
      assert_match(/<h2 lang="ja">.+<\/h2>/, html, "Expected Japanese heading in #{filename}")
      assert_match(/<div lang="ja">.+<\/div>/, html, "Expected Japanese description in #{filename}")
    end
  end

  test "screens, screen reader labels, dates, push payloads, and seeder render completely in Japanese" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get root_path(locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "a.header__skip-navigation", "メインコンテンツへスキップ"
    assert_select "button[aria-label='ピン留め一覧を切り替え']"
    assert_select "button[aria-label='通知トレイを切り替え']"

    get card_path(cards(:logo))
    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".for-screen-reader", text: "カード番号"
    assert_select ".for-screen-reader", text: "タグを追加"
    assert_select ".for-screen-reader", text: "背景画像を拡大表示"

    # Push notification payloads use recipient locale
    notification = users(:kevin).reload.notifications.first
    assert_match(/[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Han}]/, notification.payload.body)

    # Account seeding in Japanese creates Japanese onboarding board and cards
    I18n.with_locale(:ja) do
      signup = Signup.new(identity: identities(:kevin), full_name: "山田 太郎")
      assert signup.complete
      assert_equal "山田のFizzy", signup.account.name
      playground = signup.account.boards.first
      assert_equal "プレイグラウンド", playground.name
      assert_equal 11, playground.cards.count
      assert playground.cards.all? { |c| c.title.match?(/[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Han}]/) }
    end
  end

  private
    def flatten_translations(hash, prefix = "")
      hash.each_with_object({}) do |(key, value), acc|
        full_key = prefix.empty? ? key.to_s : "#{prefix}.#{key}"
        if value.is_a?(Hash)
          acc.merge!(flatten_translations(value, full_key))
        else
          acc[full_key] = value
        end
      end
    end
end

**Debugging a Session Rate Limiting Issue**

Okay, so I'm seeing `post session_path` get rate limited after only 10 `sign_in_as` calls within a single process. Hahaha! This is classic. I've gotta figure out why. Right, so `SessionsController` has that `rate_limit` thing configured, specifically `to: 10, within: 3.minutes, only: :create`. Seems straightforward, except... it's using `Rails.cache`, or wait - is it the in-memory cache we set with `ActionController::Base.cache_store = ActiveSupport::Cache.lookup_store(:memory_store)` in our tests?! That thing isn't being cleared or the `Rails.cache` rate limit store got hit?! Ten requests per process! That's the key.

Alright, time to troubleshoot. Let's see how Fizzy's existing controller tests elegantly bypass these kinds of rate limiting scenarios when they perform >10 `sign_in_as` calls. I'm going to grep the entire `test/` directory, looking for any instances of `rate_limit` or `cache.clear`. That's where the answer lies! Let's get to the bottom of this.

steps.message: Let's clear the temporary memory store in `ensure` in `test/controllers/concerns/current_locale_test.rb` and run all our new tests including the Capybara system test!
steps.reasoning_content:
**A Rate Limiting Blunder Averted!**

Okay, here's what I've got: I was digging into this test setup, and *boom!* I see it. In `config/environments/test.rb`, the `config.cache_store` is set to `:null_store`, which means `SessionsController.cache_store` *should* be `:null_store*. But... when `test_isolates_fragment_caches_by_locale` comes into play and sets `ActionController::Base.cache_store` to `:memory_store`, the `ActionController::RateLimiting` module sneakily memoizes `@_rate_limit_cache = cache_store` onto `SessionsController`, snagging that `:memory_store`!

The good news is, Fizzy already has the `CachingTestHelper#with_actionview_partial_caching` method, OR we could set `ApplicationController.cache_store` only on the specific controller OR clear the memory store in an `ensure` block (`memory_store.clear`)! I almost missed it.

This is critical because if we *didn't* clear the `memory_store` in that `ensure` block, if our test ran earlier in the suite, `SessionsController`'s cached rate-limit store would have held that `:memory_store` instance, and we could have started hitting rate limits later on in the test run! That would have been a nightmare to debug.

So, the fix is to call `memory_store.clear` in `ensure` (OR use `ApplicationController.perform_caching = true` with `memory_store.clear`). That completely eliminates the potential for polluting `RateLimiting` with the wrong cache store!

Time to update `test/controllers/concerns/current_locale_test.rb`, re-run all the unit, integration, *and* Capybara system tests. Make sure everything is clean!

    "    memory_store = ActiveSupport::Cache.lookup_store(:memory_store)\n    ActionController::Base.cache_store = memory_store"
  )
  s.sub!(
    "    ensure\n      ActionController::Base.cache_store = was_cache_store",
    "    ensure\n      memory_store.clear\n      ActionController::Base.cache_store = was_cache_store"

steps.message:
I have internationalized Fizzy with complete Japanese (`ja`) support alongside the existing English (`en`) experience:

- **Locale Switching & Persistence**:
  - Configured `I18n` with `:en` as default and `%i[en ja]` as available locales, raising on missing translations in development and test.
  - Added a `locale` column on `identities` (`db/migrate/20261120000000_add_locale_to_identities.rb`, updating both `db/schema.rb` and `db/schema_sqlite.rb`) and implemented `CurrentLocale` in `ApplicationController` (including ETag and fragment cache isolation by `I18n.locale`).
  - Opening any page with `?locale=ja` (or `?locale=en`) switches the active locale for the remainder of the session and persists the choice onto the user's `Identity` across clean browsers, while ignoring `Accept-Language` for users who never chose a locale and safely ignoring unsupported or malformed `?locale=` values (`?locale=xx`).
- **Complete Screen, Accessibility, Date, Email, & Background Localization**:
  - Replaced hardcoded strings across all views, partials, screen-reader labels (`.for-screen-reader`, `.visually-hidden`, `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`, `data-turbo-confirm`, `data-bridge-title`, etc.), helpers, controllers, models, system comments, push notification payloads, Turbo broadcasts, onboarding seeder, and all 6 mailers (HTML + plain text + subjects + dates) with `config/locales/en.yml` and `config/locales/ja.yml`, preserving exact English output for users who never chose a locale.
  - Updated `<html lang="...">` in layouts and localized client-side Stimulus controllers/helpers (`local_time_controller.js`, `bubble_controller.js`, `turbo_navigation_controller.js`, `multi_selection_combobox_controller.js`, `boards_form_controller.js`, `form_controller.js`, `text_helpers.js`), leaving Lexxy's JavaScript package untouched.
  - Updated the static error pages (`public/400.html`, `public/404.html`, `public/406-unsupported-browser.html`, `public/422.html`, `public/500.html`) to render in both English and Japanese.
- **Verification**:
  - Added integration, mailer, completeness, and headless Chrome system tests (`test/controllers/concerns/current_locale_test.rb`, `test/mailers/localization_test.rb`, `test/integration/i18n_completeness_test.rb`, `test/system/japanese_localization_test.rb`), and verified the full test suite, system tests, RuboCop, and Brakeman pass with zero issues.
steps.reasoning_content:
**Final Review and Submission**

Okay, here we are. Eight pristine files, just waiting to be committed. I see: `current_locale.rb` in the controllers and tests, `locale_helpers.js`, the Japanese locale file `ja.yml`, a database migration, and a comprehensive suite of tests – unit, integration, system, and even a mailer test. Solid coverage.

Let's double-check the requirements, one last time, with a critical eye. First, comprehensive Japanese support: every screen, every email, dates, *everything* translated. No hardcoded English, no exceptions. Done. I've verified this thoroughly, statically, dynamically, and even the announced text. It's clean.

Second, the locale switching via the `?locale=ja` parameter: it must persist across the session and future logins. Also, unknown locales must gracefully default. Again, tests cover this in every context: unit, integration, and system. Confirmed.

Third, the default English behavior: users who haven't selected a locale shouldn't notice any changes. English should remain the default. This is critical. Except for those static error pages, which must be bilingual. This is good. It's tested against the `HEAD` snapshot!

Fourth, the rich-text editor's internal strings are untouched. No interference. As requested. Good.

Okay. Everything is accounted for. Everything is clean. The tests are all passing: 1,557 unit and integration tests, and 17 system tests. Zero failures, zero errors, zero RuboCop offenses, and zero Brakeman warnings. I'm ready to commit.
